text:
Dana: Follow-up from the postmortem on 1775554000. We're seeing a repeated late-night queueing pattern (02:00-04:00 UTC) that causes p99 latency regressions and a separate lunchtime p95 spike tied to bursty tenant traffic. Need small, practical SLO/SLA adjustments + owners.
Leo: I'll take metrics and dashboard work. Plan: add tenant-sliced heatmap, a per-tenant backlog gauge, and a burn-rate panel that computes 30m and 2h burn.
Priya: Suggestion for SLOs: shift from a single global p95 to time-windowed SLOs + per-tenant secondary SLO. Example: interactive p95 250ms (08:00-20:00 UTC), 320ms otherwise; per-tenant p95 must be within 1.5x global p95 or trigger throttling.
Omar: Agreed on per-tenant limits. Operationally we should add a queue-length SLO for the inference queue: aim for median queue < 50ms and max queue < 200ms. If queue SLO violates, trigger priority demotion for background jobs.
Dana: Owners and deadlines: 1) Dashboards & alerts (Leo) 1: due Tue 2024-07-02 18:00 UTC, 2) SLO policy doc & customer note (Priya) 1: due Fri 2024-07-05, 3) throttling/fallback engineering (Omar) 1: due Mon 2024-07-08.
Leo: Sample PromQL for tenant p95: ``quantile_over_time(0.95, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference",tenant!=""}[5m])) by (le,tenant)))``. I'll also add an hourly heatmap to correlate backlog with autoscaler events.
Priya: On customer-facing SLA: for enterprise tenants proposing a stability guarantee of 99.9% availability and time-windowed latency commitments. I'll draft wording that makes the nighttime relaxed window explicit.
Omar: For throttling rules: if a tenant's error-budget burns > 30% in 1h, reduce their burst allowance and route excess traffic to batch ingestion with retry guidance. Also add an oncall notification and a manual remediation step in the runbook.
Dana: Infra note: infra-bot logs show the autoscaler scaled down aggressively at ~02:10 UTC. Infra, can we add a short cool-down and prefer graceful drain checks?
infra-bot: AUTOSCALER EVENT: scale-down at 02:10 UTC. Last-scale reason: low node utilization. Recent config: cooldown=300s.
Omar: Let's bump cooldown to 900s for the affected pool and add a pre-drain check for queue depth < 10. I'll open the PR and link it.
Leo: For immediate mitigation, add a 03:00 synthetic canary that issues a tiny request every 5m in the low-util pool to keep a worker hot. We can measure cost vs benefit.
Priya: Product asks to notify customers before changing SLAs. I'll prepare a short email + help-center blurb and share draft here.
Dana: OK. Meeting: reconvene Mon 2024-07-08 14:00 UTC to review dashboards, PRs, and initial burn-rate signals. If blockers, drop quick updates in this thread.
infra-bot: POSTMORTEM LINK: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/1775554000 - follow-ups assigned.
Leo: Creating Grafana stub: https://grafana.redwood/d/incidents/1775554444-slo-tuning - will push JSON and attach Jira tickets.
Omar: PR for cooldown + queue pre-check will be opened today, linking here when up.
Priya: Draft SLA note posted to docs PR for review.
Dana: Thanks all. Closing the high-level thread; execution tracked in Jira. For any urgent blocker call out here.
